questions.def: Causative 'have' requires past participle for completed action.
questions.question: I had the report ___ by Friday.

questions.def: 'Get' causative needs past participle for completed action.
questions.question: She got her article ___ in the journal.

questions.def: 'Have' causative needs past participle after the object.
questions.question: I will ___ my car tomorrow.

questions.def: 'Have' causative means someone else did the action.
questions.question: They had their house ___ after the storm.

questions.def: 'Get' causative implies someone else performed the action.
questions.question: We got the documents ___ by a notary.

questions.def: 'Have' causative needs past participle after the object.
questions.question: She ___ the letter into French.

questions.def: Passive causative, 'have' + object + past participle.
questions.question: I had my eyes ___ yesterday.

questions.def: Passive causative, 'get' + object + past participle.
questions.question: He got his proposal ___ by the committee.

questions.def: Causative 'have' + object + past participle.
questions.question: She ___ her manuscript by an expert.

questions.def: 'Get' + object + past participle: someone else did it.
questions.question: We got the system ___ by the engineers.

questions.def: 'Have' + object + past participle for passive causative.
questions.question: They had the software ___ to the latest version.

questions.def: Causative 'have' + object + past participle.
questions.question: He ___ his watch.

questions.def: 'Get' causative implies action done by someone else.
questions.question: She got the article ___.

questions.def: 'Make' causative uses base form of the verb.
questions.question: The manager made him ___ the report.

questions.def: 'Have' causative requires past participle after object.
questions.question: They ___ their work.

questions.def: 'Have' + object + past participle for passive action.
questions.question: The company had the building ___.

questions.def: 'Get' + object + past participle for passive causative.
questions.question: I got my computer ___ by a technician.

questions.def: Causative 'have' uses past participle after the object.
questions.question: He ___ the contract.

questions.def: 'Get' causative and past participle show completed action.
questions.question: We got the problem ___ quickly.

questions.def: 'Make' causative uses base form without 'to'.
questions.question: The director made the actors ___ their lines.

questions.def: 'Have' causative requires past participle after object.
questions.question: I ___ the documents.

questions.def: 'Get' causative implies someone else is doing the action.
questions.question: She got her visa ___ in time.

questions.def: 'Have' causative requires past participle after object.
questions.question: They had the article ___ in the journal.

questions.def: With 'have' as a causative, the bare infinitive is used after the object.
questions.question: I had him ___ the report immediately.

questions.def: 'Get' as a causative requires a past participle to show the action was done.
questions.question: She got her car ___ yesterday.

questions.def: 'Make' as a causative takes the bare infinitive, not the 'to' infinitive.
questions.question: They made him to confess, despite his initial denial.

questions.def: Reflexive causative: get/have something done. 'Have' shows it's habitually done.
questions.question: I ___ my house every Saturday.

questions.def: 'Had' + object + past participle indicates the action was performed by someone else.
questions.question: Having had the document ___, he filed it away.

questions.def: 'Have' (causative) + object + past participle indicates passive voice: action is done.
questions.question: We must have the system ___ immediately.

questions.def: 'Let' requires the bare infinitive, not the 'to' infinitive.
questions.question: She let the children to stay up late last night.
